title: Adaptive microkernel ranking + time-windowed prefill/decode handshake for mixed-MIG pods
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: On multi-tenant clusters with mixed GPU types (H100, L40S, A10) and MIG partitioning we see frequent suboptimal kernel choices during prefill -> decode handoffs. Prefill batches often select kernels optimized for throughput but that require higher clocks or different memory patterns; when the decode stage is scheduled on a smaller MIG slice or a different frequency domain we observe stalls, p99 latency spikes, and increased thermal throttling.

Goal: Implement an adaptive microkernel ranking and a time-windowed prefill/decode handshake so that the scheduler selects kernel variants compatible with downstream constraints (MIG slice size, current clock headroom, thermal state) and avoids decode stalls. This should improve p99 latency and end-to-end tokens/sec for mixed-MIG workloads without increasing overall power significantly.

High-level approach:
- Add a per-model microkernel scoring table populated from lightweight microbenchmarks (tokens/sec, p99, memory footprint, transient power).
- Score kernels by weighted utility that includes hardware-affinity constraints (MIG slice capabilities, SM count), current clock headroom, and decode latency sensitivity (configured per route/model).
- Implement a time-windowed handshake between prefill and decode: prefill will reserve a short decode window on the same affinity class or request an aligned MIG slice when feasible. If the handshake fails within N ms, prefill falls back to a conservative kernel variant that is compatible with more constrained decode environments.
- Expose a clock-headroom hint to the runtime's clock governor for brief boosts during the reserved decode window for workloads with high decode sensitivity. This is opt-in per deployment class (dedicated/private only; hosted will be conservative).
- Instrument telemetry: kernel_choice, kernel_score_breakdown, handshake_latency, fallback_count, p99_by_route, power_draw_estimate. Use these to drive online updates to the microkernel ranking.

Design constraints and trade-offs:
- Safety: avoid aggressive clock increases for shared-hosted tenants. Clock boost only enabled for Dedicated/Private with admin opt-in.
- Complexity: keep handshake lightweight to avoid adding latency for the common fast path.
- Correctness: ensure KV cache usage and memory layouts stay compatible between kernel variants; add validation in the kernel adaptor.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: full autotuning pipeline for all model families (follow-up), quantization-specific kernel exploration (separate effort).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Microkernel scoring table exists for H100/L40S/A10 and is populated from an automated microbench job.
2) Scheduler picks a kernel variant based on the scoring function and hardware affinity during prefill for at least 3 representative routes.
3) Time-windowed handshake implemented: prefill can reserve a decode slot and handshake success/failure is recorded.
4) Fallback path to conservative kernel triggers when handshake fails, with no request failures.
5) Telemetry dashboards show kernel_choice, handshake_latency, fallback_count.
6) Canary rollout demonstrates >=10% tokens/sec improvement and p99 latency reduction >=12ms on mixed-MIG synthetic workload compared to baseline, without >5% sustained increase in power draw on Dedicated clusters.
7) Unit and integration tests for kernel adaptor compatibility and handshake edge cases are present and passing in CI.
notes: Implementation will touch: runtime/batcher, runtime/scheduler, kernel-adaptor, telemetry pipeline, and ops-runbooks for clock hinting. We will coordinate with infra to expose MIG slice topology & current clock headroom via host agent. Project will be split across two PRs: core scoring + scheduler changes, then optional clock hinting and enabling for Dedicated clusters.
comments: 2025-11-21: Triage completed. Assigned to Miguel. Initial bench harness prototype exists in perf/benchmkr-2025. Link to prototype logs: https://internal.redwood/perf/bench/benchmkr-2025/hybrid-mig-run

2025-11-25: Design review notes — PM asked we quantify customer scenarios (short chat vs long generations). Decided to prioritize short chat workloads for first pass. See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RUNTIME/Microkernel+Ranking+Design
2025-11-30: Eng sync — infra (ENG-90412) needs a host-agent change to report per-slice clock headroom. Marked as dependency. Also flagged thermal-signal API gaps for hosted tenants (ENG-90501).

2025-12-03: Prototype microbench completed for H100 and L40S. Preliminary scoring shows H100 strong variants with +14% tokens/sec but also 8% higher instantaneous power. We added weight for power in the scoring formula to avoid regressing thermal behavior.

2025-12-05: Implementation PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289. Core scheduler + scoring merged to staging. Clock hinting PR is gated behind infra rollout. Starting canary on Dedicated cluster 'eu-west-2-dedicated-3'.
